alt: A title banner in black and bright turquoise reads "AN OPEN LETTER / TO ANYONE WHO IS SUFFERING AFTER A RAPE." Below, a short-haired person in glasses and a turquoise t-shirt turns toward the reader with both hands open, speaking from a large speech balloon; a black ribbon at the bottom reads "BY ELIZABETH BEIER."
text:
AN OPEN LETTER
TO ANYONE WHO IS SUFFERING AFTER A RAPE
FIRST OF ALL, I AM SO, SO SORRY YOU WERE RAPED. I'M NOT HERE TO TELL YOU WHAT YOU SHOULD DO — NO ONE CAN TELL YOU THAT — BUT TO OFFER WHAT HELPED ME THE MOST.
BY ELIZABETH BEIER

alt: A banner asks "WHAT are you FEELING right now?" above a large cracked heart split down the middle: the bright turquoise left half is lettered FEAR, SHAME and RAGE over drawn mountains, the dark grey-green right half is lettered Sadness, numbness and NOTHING over cracked ground. Black clouds along the bottom carry white text about the feelings being valid.
text:
WHAT are you FEELING right now?
FEAR
SHAME
RAGE
Sadness
numbness
NOTHING
NO MATTER THE ANSWER, YOUR FEELINGS ARE VALID AND I HOPE YOU TREAT YOURSELF WITH GENTLENESS.

alt: A wide-eyed person holds their hands up as their words, "HELLO?" and "ARE YOU ALL RIGHT?", curve away in wobbling turquoise ribbons toward a second figure trapped inside a black blob, pressing outward with both palms and thinking "WHERE AM I?". A turquoise caption box beneath gives a grounding exercise.
text:
SOMETIMES YOU MIGHT FEEL DISORIENTED AND DISSOCIATED FROM THE WORLD. FOR ME, THAT WAS THE SCARIEST PART.
HELLO?
ARE YOU ALL RIGHT?
WHERE AM I?
PLANT BOTH FEET ON THE GROUND AND COUNT THINGS AROUND YOU. HOW MANY RED THINGS DO YOU SEE? HOW MANY METAL THINGS? COUNTING CAN BRING YOU BACK TO THE PRESENT.

alt: A dark-haired woman with her eyes closed sits calmly at the center while pale turquoise memories stream out of her hair like smoke — two friends laughing "HA HA HA HA HA HA!", a girl in pigtails holding an ice cream cone, a palm-lined beach, a figure hiking toward mountains at sunrise — all set against faint jagged shapes. Captions above and below explain the idea.
text:
TO PREPARE FOR THE TIMES WHEN FEAR, ANXIETY AND SADNESS EMERGE...
HA HA HA HA HA HA!
...BUILD A MENTAL LIBRARY OF YOUR MOST COMFORTING AND JOYFUL MEMORIES — AND EVERY TIME YOU CHECK THEM OUT, LET THEM GET RICHER IN DETAIL.

alt: Two friends sit facing each other on a big turquoise couch holding mugs — one cross-legged in a polka-dot top and sneakers, the other in a vest, skirt and tall boots with a shaved-side haircut and a choker. A large caption box above them talks about telling trusted people how you really feel.
text: IF THERE ARE PEOPLE IN YOUR LIFE WHO LISTEN AND ARE THERE FOR YOU NO MATTER WHAT, TELL THEM HOW YOU REALLY FEEL AND WHAT YOU REALLY NEED. THEY MIGHT NOT ALWAYS SAY THE RIGHT THING, WHICH CAN BE PAINFUL, BUT HAVING A SUPPORT NETWORK CAN REALLY HELP.

alt: At night, a small lone figure stands at the bottom of a glowing turquoise path, shading her eyes to look up a steep grey mountain tangled with dark thorny brambles; a tiny lit flag marks the distant summit under a starry sky. A white caption box floats at the upper left.
text: FROM WHERE YOU'RE STANDING NOW, I KNOW IT CAN BE HARD TO BELIEVE THAT YOU WILL FEEL BETTER AGAIN ONE DAY.

alt: The same mountain path in daylight and pale blue: a smiling woman stands at the summit beside a planted flag, one arm swept out toward clouds and sunbeams. Text in the lower right invites the reader to picture their future self.
text: SO INSTEAD, TAKE A MINUTE TO IMAGINE BEING THE FUTURE YOU, WHO IS LIVING AN AWESOME LIFE. WHAT DO YOU DO EVERY DAY AND HOW DOES IT FEEL?

alt: Two versions of the same woman embrace against a glowing turquoise and near-black night sky flecked with stars; one holds the other close with her eyes closed, both drawn in luminous outline. A white caption box at the top poses a question.
text: WHAT WOULD FUTURE YOU SAY TO PRESENT YOU?

alt: A hand-lettered turquoise note fills the panel, headed "READER," with a pale drawn hand holding a brush at the lower right as if it has just written the words. Small black text under the note points to a hotline and resources.
text:
READER,
I HOPE THIS HELPED. WHOEVER YOU ARE, WHEREVER YOU ARE, I BELIEVE YOU AND I BELIEVE IN YOU.
- ELIZABETH
FOR MORE RESOURCES AND A 24-HOUR HOTLINE, PLEASE VISIT RAINN.ORG
